finding.claim: The client connects to the named pipe without verifying the server's identity, so a local unprivileged user can pre-create the predictable pipe name while Pageant is not running and intercept the victim's SSH agent requests, returning forged identities or failing signatures. Low severity; plausible, not verified at runtime.
finding.source: Local unprivileged attacker on the same Windows host. Pipe name built from the caller's username (UPN or SAM name) and a deterministic SHA-256 suffix over CryptProtectMemory of 'Pageant'.
finding.sink: ClientOptions::new().open(&pipe_name) in PageantStream::new, which sends SSH agent requests (including sign requests) to whichever process owns the pipe.

trace.note: get_username obtains the username via GetUserNameExA, falling back to GetUserNameA
capi_obfuscate_string gives a deterministic suffix (CryptProtectMemory CROSS_PROCESS over 'Pageant', SHA-256)
open(&pipe_name) connects with no server ownership or identity check
A non-busy error returns immediately; if the attacker holds the pipe, the client talks to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Pipe name is not secret, so guessing is not the barrier. No GetNamedPipeServerProcessId or server-owner check exists. Pageant's own pipe creation would fail once the attacker holds the name. Exploit needs a local account and Pageant to be stopped. Impact is request interception and forged responses, not private-key extraction, because keys stay in the agent.

finding.claim: find_pageant_window locates the agent by window class and title 'Pageant' only, so any process in the same desktop session that registers a window with that class and title can receive WM_COPYDATA requests and return forged responses. Low severity; plausible, not verified on Windows. Same-user malware already has key access, so the real exposure is lower-integrity or sandboxed processes that can open the mapping.
finding.source: Any local process in the same desktop session that creates a top-level window with class 'Pageant' and title 'Pageant'.
finding.sink: SendMessageA(WM_COPYDATA) in query_pageant_direct, which delivers the request mapping name to the window owner. The response is then read from the shared mapping and trusted by the caller.

trace.note: find_pageant_window calls FindWindowW with class 'Pageant' and title 'Pageant' and returns the first match
MemoryMap::new creates the request mapping 'PageantRequest<cookie>' with the default DACL
The request message is written into the shared mapping
SendMessageA(WM_COPYDATA) passes the mapping name to whichever window was found
The response is read from the shared mapping, with the size taken from the peer and bounds-checked at read()

finding.guards_checked: Bounds checks in read() and write() prevent out-of-range access. No check confirms the window owner's process identity or executable path. Cross-user spoofing is not possible across window stations. Whether a sandboxed process can open the mapping under the default DACL and integrity label was not verified.
